description.narrative:
Promoting Independent Media and Freedom of Expression in Cambodia is crucial to enhance transparency, democratic accountability, inclusive public participation, and oversight in public financial management. Limited awareness, access to equipment, and technical training on digital and media literacy, rise of misinformation and disinformation weakens public engagement and policy responses. By producing a suite of media products including radio shows, videos, and news articles to inform Cambodian citizens –particularly youth, women, and marginalised groups to be more informed and actively engage in monitoring and participation in local budget applicationand expenditure and improved citizen engagement in government policy formulation, enforcement and strengthen good governance and democracy. All public interest contents will be posted on WMC website and/or social media platforms.
This project aimed to achieve the following outcomes:
1) Cambodian citizens particularly youth, women, and marginalised groups including indiginous people become more inform and actively engage in budget transparency, accountability, and oversight in public financial management through the production and distribution of public interest contents. 2) Cambodian citizens particularly youth, women, and marginalised groups including indiginous people become more informed and actively involved in advocating for budget transparency, accountability, and oversight in public financial management through training on media and information literacy and fact-checking. 3) Cambodian citizens particularly youth, women, and marginalised groups including indiginous people increased in the number of reporting leaning to greater involvement in monitoring and participating in local budget allocation and expenditure through the production of news contents and dissemintation through social media platforms.

participating-org.narrative:
Novib supports the Women’s Media Centre of Cambodia since 1996. Novib is a long time stable core funder. Other donors support WMC on a project basis. WMC is the primary NGO in Cambodia addressing women's issues through the media, and an important source of information for many Cambodians, especially about the challenges women face.
The Women's Media Centre of Cambodia (WMC) was established as a non-profit, non-governmental organization in January 1995 with Council of Ministers and with Ministry of Interior in 2001. In recognition of its changing management needs, WMC has successfully reformed its organizational structure in early 2007 from led by Co-Directors to an Executive Director.
Since its foundation, WMC has produced multi media approaches and innovative high quality radio, television and video productions, designs, electronic communication and website to educate and inform Cambodians on a wide range of issues impacting on women’s rights and human rights, reproductive health, HIV/AIDS, trafficking, elections, domestic violence, leadership, sexual assaults, drug abuse, rule of law, decentralization, poverty, Civil Society Dialogue and Public Awareness Raising, rape, land dispute/conflicts etc.
The Women’s Media Centre of Cambodia occupies aunique position among Cambodian NGOs and media organizations. It is the only media organization managed and run by women, and the only NGO with a focus on women and the media. The WMC develops, produces and broadcasts integrated media campaigns on social issues affecting women and men, and has considerable expertise in social change campaigning.
Today, WMC continues to use the mass media to promote social change in Cambodian society. The center run by women as majority has become the foremost providers of public service broadcasting in the country. Through independent and civil society radio, television and video productions, WMC has addressed nearly every issue affecting women in Cambodia. Some of the issues include health, reproductive health, HIV,TB, Malaria, trafficking of women and children, leadership, national elections, domestic violence, good governance, decentralization, road of law, justice and poverty. Additionally, the center has also provided evident-based information, education and advice to a broad range of audiences, both male and female.
The Women’s Media Center of Cambodia (WMC) has provided, broadcasted and aired to advocate and inform public for changing the policy, guidelines, norms, practices,as well as long-term and sustainable behaviors of marginalized people, most-at-risk population, disadvantaged groups, and vulnerable children and women in particular.
WMC is an independent and non-partisan Cambodia Women’s Media Organization dedicated to improving the status of women in Cambodia. Its mission is: ? To use the media services to educate, lobby and increase awareness of women’s rights in Cambodian Society. ? To use the media services to empower women by providing evident-based information on socio-economic issues impacting their lives, and by giving them a voice on these issues; ? To advocate for the positive portrayal of women in the public media, and to encourage and support women in media professions.
